analysis: The changed files are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (scheduler prefill geometry table around lines 1087-1090, 1100-1146, and invariants 8-9 at lines 2028-2041) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (lines 324 and 534-540). No executable code, wire contracts, keys, attestation paths, or authorization logic change in this diff. The documentation describes a wider default prefill chunk (2048 tokens, with a 4096 step) for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5/3.8 and Gemma 4. It also describes a 512-token media chunk ceiling, and a consequence for durable prefix-cache boundaries: under decode company, a dense Qwen donor leaves no durable boundary in a prompt shorter than 2048 tokens. That is a performance and cache-hit trade-off. It does not widen the at-rest exposure in T-041. The cacheSalt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, disk budgets, and KEK purge posture are unchanged. The unit with the patch excerpt (docs/architecture/inference.md) was truncated, so the table rows beyond line 1090 and the line 1100-1146 region were not visible in full. The cited code (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift prefillGeometry/usesWidePrefillChunk, SchedulerV2 prefillChunkCap) is not supplied, so whether the real behavior matches the documentation is unverified. Possible availability or memory effects of wider prefill chunks (T-029 and the memory admission paths) belong to the code change that sits outside this documentation-only batch. Wider chunks could increase peak transient memory, and the documentation states that the existing admission gates remain in force. I identified no security regression or threat-model invalidation from these documentation changes. The integration pass should check whether any companion code changes in the PR alter the cache or admission behavior.
